subject: On-prem networking: surge readiness & segmentation checklist for ACME private deploy
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>, CloudOps Team <cloudops@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem networking: surge readiness & segmentation checklist for ACME private deploy

Tom / CloudOps —

We ran the lane-assignments this morning and want to confirm the operational posture for the private deployment cutover next week. Two specific asks before we lock the window:

1) Surge capacity behavior: when ACME’s ingest spikes (simulated at 3x baseline), we need clarity on how your edge LB/ingress will shape backpressure to avoid connection storms to the control plane. Do you intend to drop or buffer at the edge, and do you have a preferred concurrency limit per upstream neighbor?

2) Segmentation + egress matrix: we propose a minimal egress allowlist for telemetry and NTP, plus an optional debug tunnel to GlobalInfra for failfast diagnostics. I attached a draft connectivity diagram (acme_vpc_connectivity_v2.png) and an initial segmentation spreadsheet. Please review ports and suggested CIDR ranges.

Operational constraints we need to validate on our side:
- Control-plane heartbeat TTL and retries (default propose: 5s heartbeat, 3 retries)
- KV cache warmup window per rack (we're seeing ~800ms cold-start per model shard)
- Canary routing policy for 1% of traffic to dedicated pool during cutover

Can you confirm the edge behavior and whether you can open the peer ACLs below? If helpful we can run a 90-minute tabletop on Friday with your engineers + Kimberly/Irene.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra PM — Redwood Inference
[attachment: acme_vpc_connectivity_v2.png (image/png)]
[attachment: segmentation-egress-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, CloudOps Team <cloudops@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem networking: surge readiness & segmentation checklist for ACME private deploy

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline:

1) Surge behavior: we will buffer up to 60 seconds per connection at the edge LB (FQDN-based routing), then apply connection caps per upstream of 100 concurrent connections by default. We can increase to 250 for the dedicated pool during the 3-day cutover window — we just need notification 48hrs prior to lock changes.

2) Egress: NTP (udp/123), telemetry (tcp/443 -> telemetry.acme.com), and S3 endpoints are fine. For the debug tunnel to GlobalInfra we need a signed NDA because it transits a third-party datacenter.

We reviewed the attached diagram and flagged two firewall rules that need refinement (see comments in segmentation-egress-matrix.xlsx). Also: please confirm the control-plane heartbeat proposal — the edge LB will treat a missing heartbeat as a soft-fail after 20s of consecutive misses unless you set the TTL to be longer.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Cloud Infrastructure Lead — Acme Corp
[attachment: acme_edge_fw_comments.txt (text)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem networking: surge readiness & segmentation checklist for ACME private deploy

Tom / team —

Appreciate the quick review. A few follow-ups from our runbook and security constraints: 

- Control-plane heartbeats: we can align to your suggestion if we increase retry/backoff logic on the client side. Proposed final: 5s heartbeat, exponential backoff (2x), max retry window 25s; if exceeded, client falls back to model-serving-only mode (no control plane ops).

- KV cache: we'll pre-warm model shards for the first 10% of traffic during the canary phase; expected warmup per shard ~700-900ms depending on model. We'll add a separate KV replication lane (intra-rack) to reduce cross-rack hits.

- Egress & observability: Redwood needs to be allowed tcp/443 to telemetry.acme.com and tcp/443 to s3.acme-region-1.amazonaws.com — we will use cert-pinned endpoints. For auditing please ensure FlowLogs are stored for 90 days in the project bucket.

Action items:
- Tom: confirm NDA timeline for GlobalInfra debug tunnel (Y/N)
- Aditya: schedule a Friday 90-minute tabletop (include GW + infra + ops)
- Jonas: prepare 1% canary routing policy and cutover checklist (draft attached)

Kimberly Park
Head of Deployments — Redwood Inference
[attachment: cutover-checklist.md (markdown)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-08T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem networking: surge readiness & segmentation checklist for ACME private deploy

All —

I spun up the proposed canary policy and a short cutover playbook in the ops repo. Summary:

- Canary: 1% traffic routed to dedicated pool for 4 hours, metrics checked every 15m (latency, 5xx rate, token cost delta). Auto-rollback on sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 30m.
- Surge mitigation: client-side concurrency limiter set to 200 during cutover window; we will coordinate with Tom to bump edge LB to 250 as needed.
- Diagnostics: we will only enable the GlobalInfra debug tunnel after NDA is signed; until then, we will stream compressed traces to the telemetry endpoint (no raw payload).

Cutover window proposal: Tue 2027-04-13 02:00-06:00 UTC (low traffic; Redwood on-call + ACME CloudOps present). Please confirm by EOD Monday so we can put the ACL change request in.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
